title: Satan as a Created Being
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Satan is a created spiritual being who became a rebel against God through pride and sin. He was not created evil, is not equal with God, and remains under God’s sovereign authority and limitation.
summary: Satan is a created spiritual being who became a rebel against God through pride and sin. He was not created evil, is not equal with God, and remains under God’s sovereign authority and limitation.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is infinitely greater than Satan. Christ came to destroy the works of the devil, defeat his condemning power, and rescue sinners from darkness through His death, resurrection, and reign.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Satan is not eternal, divine, or equal with God. He is a created being. Everything God made was under His authority, and no creature exists independently from Him. Satan’s existence does not challenge God’s sovereignty.

God did not create Satan evil. Scripture teaches that angels sinned and that some did not keep their proper place. Satan became the adversary through rebellion, pride, deception, and opposition to God.

Satan is powerful, but he is limited. He deceives, accuses, tempts, and opposes the work of God, but he cannot overthrow God’s plan. He is never presented as the dark equal of God.

Christ’s victory is the believer’s confidence. Jesus came to destroy the works of the devil. Through the cross and resurrection, He breaks Satan’s condemning power and rescues sinners from darkness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people talk about Satan as though he is equal with God, while others treat him like a myth. Scripture avoids both errors. Satan is real and dangerous, but he is created, fallen, limited, and defeated by Christ.

This doctrine also protects believers from fear and confusion. Spiritual evil is serious, but it is not ultimate. The believer stands in Christ, who is Lord over all.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Take Satan seriously without fearing him as though he were sovereign. Do not blame God for Satan’s rebellion, and do not treat darkness as equal with the Lord. Submit to God, resist the devil, trust Christ’s victory, and stay anchored in Scripture rather than speculation, fear, or obsession.
